sentences.nl: Vandaag is de achtste finale van de Champions League, tussen Ajax en AC Milaan.
sentences.en: Today is the round of 16 of the Champions League, between Ajax and AC Milan.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Today is the eighth final of the Champions League, between Ajax and AC Milan.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Vandaag is" (Today is): "Vandaag" is an adverb of time, and in Dutch, it often comes at the beginning of the sentence, followed by the verb.  
• "de achtste finale" (the eighth final): "Achtste" is an ordinal number meaning "eighth."  
• "van de Champions League" (of the Champions League): "van" is a preposition meaning "of," used to show possession or association.  
• "tussen Ajax en AC Milaan" (between Ajax and AC Milan): "Tussen" is a preposition meaning "between," used for spatial or metaphorical positioning.  
• Extra phrases:  
  - "Morgen is de eerste wedstrijd van het seizoen." (Tomorrow is the first match of the season.)  
  - "De derde verdieping van het gebouw is gesloten." (The third floor of the building is closed.)  
  - "Het gesprek was tussen de directeur en de manager." (The conversation was between the director and the manager.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Volgende week is de halve finale van het toernooi, tussen Nederland en België. (Next week is the semi-final of the tournament, between the Netherlands and Belgium.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The Champions League is a prestigious annual club football competition organized by the Union of European Football Associations (UEFA). It is highly popular in the Netherlands, especially when a local team like Ajax participates.

sentences.nl: En Marieke is boos op Gianluca, door een foute opmerking.
sentences.en: And Marieke is angry with Gianluca because of a wrong remark.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And Marieke is angry at Gianluca, because of a wrong comment.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Boos op" is a fixed expression meaning "angry at." The preposition "op" is used to indicate the target of the anger.  
• "Door een foute opmerking" means "because of a wrong comment," where "door" indicates causation or reason.  
• Word order: Dutch typically places the main verb ("is") in the second position, following the subject ("Marieke").  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Hij is boos op mij." (He is angry at me.)  
  - "Door het slechte weer gingen we niet." (Because of the bad weather, we did not go.)  
  - "Ze was boos op haar broer." (She was angry at her brother.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• En Pieter is boos op zijn collega, door een misverstand. (And Pieter is angry at his colleague, because of a misunderstanding.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• There are no specific cultural notes for this sentence.

sentences.nl: Allemaal erg gezellig,, maar nu ben je tegen mijn club Ajax.
sentences.en: All very nice, but now you are against my club Ajax.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• All very cozy, but now you are against my club Ajax.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The word "allemaal" is used to indicate "all" or "everything," often to introduce a general statement.  
• "Gezellig" is a quintessential Dutch word meaning cozy, fun, or pleasant. It's used to describe a pleasant atmosphere or situation.  
• The phrase "je tegen" indicates opposition, with "tegen" meaning "against."  
• Sentence structure with "maar" (but) introduces a contrast or exception.

• Examples:  
  - "Allemaal leuk en aardig, maar ik moet gaan." (All nice and fine, but I have to go.)  
  - "Het was gezellig, maar ik ben moe." (It was cozy, but I am tired.)  
  - "Je bent tegen mij, dat weet ik." (You are against me, I know that.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Allemaal heel leuk, maar ik heb geen tijd." (All very nice, but I have no time.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• "Ajax" is one of the most famous football clubs in the Netherlands, based in Amsterdam. Football is a significant part of Dutch culture, and club loyalty can be strong and passionate.

sentences.nl: Ik haat Ajax.
sentences.en: I hate Ajax.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I hate Ajax.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ik" means "I" and is the subject pronoun.  
• "Haat" is the present tense form of the verb "haten," meaning "to hate."  
• "Ajax" is a proper noun, referring to the popular Dutch football club based in Amsterdam.

• Examples:  
  - Ik haat regen. (I hate rain.)  
  - Zij haat het vroege opstaan. (She hates getting up early.)  
  - Wij haten lawaai. (We hate noise.)  

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Ik haat koude koffie. (I hate cold coffee.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, football is a very popular sport, and clubs like Ajax have passionate supporters and rivals. Expressing strong opinions about football teams is common and can be part of friendly banter among fans.

sentences.nl: Ik ben altijd voor de ploeg die tegen Ajax speelt.
sentences.en: I always support the team that plays against Ajax.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I am always for the team that against Ajax plays.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ik ben altijd voor" means "I am always for" or "I always support." The structure "ben voor" indicates support or preference.  
• "de ploeg die tegen Ajax speelt" means "the team that plays against Ajax." "Die" is a relative pronoun referring to "de ploeg" (the team).  
• The verb "speelt" is in the present tense, appropriate for describing ongoing or habitual actions.

• Extra examples:  
  - "Ik ben altijd voor de underdog." (I am always for the underdog.)  
  - "Hij is tegen de plannen die de regering maakt." (He is against the plans that the government makes.)  
  - "Zij support de club die in de finale speelt." (She supports the club that plays in the final.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Hij juicht altijd voor de ploeg die tegen Feyenoord speelt. (He always cheers for the team that plays against Feyenoord.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Ajax is a prominent football club in the Netherlands, based in Amsterdam. Supporting teams playing against Ajax could indicate local rivalries, as Ajax is often seen as a dominant team in the Dutch league.

sentences.nl: Ik vind dat een beetje raar.
sentences.en: I find that a bit strange.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I find that a bit strange.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ik vind" (I find) is a common way to express an opinion in Dutch. "Vind" is the first-person singular present tense of "vinden" (to find).  
• "Dat" (that) is a demonstrative pronoun here, referring to something previously mentioned or understood.  
• "Een beetje" (a bit) is used to soften the statement, similar to "a little" in English.  
• "Raar" (strange) is an adjective meaning odd or unusual.  
• Example: "Ik vind het leuk." (I find it nice/I like it.)  
• Example: "Dat is een beetje te veel." (That is a bit too much.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Ik vind dat erg interessant." (I find that very interesting.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, being direct is common, but using terms like "een beetje" can soften opinions or criticisms, making them more acceptable in social interactions.

• "Nog eentje" can be translated as "yet one" or "another one," with "nog" indicating "yet" or "still," and "eentje" being a diminutive form of "één," meaning "one."  
• The diminutive form "eentje" is often used for emphasis or affection.  
• Example sentences:

sentences.nl: Jij bent toch docent Nederlands? — Kun je lesgeven aan mij? — Mijn Nederlands is nog niet zo goed.

sentences.nl: Wanneer? — Misschien nu? — Martin wordt een beetje jaloers…
sentences.en: When? — Maybe now? — Martin is getting a little jealous…
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• When? — Maybe now? — Martin becomes a little jealous...

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Wanneer?" is a question word meaning "When?"  
• "Misschien" means "maybe" and is used to express uncertainty or possibility.  
• "Nu" means "now," indicating the present time.  
• "Wordt" is the present tense of "worden," meaning "to become."  
• "Een beetje" means "a little," used to indicate a small amount.  
• "Jaloers" means "jealous," an adjective describing someone's feelings.

Extra Phrases:  
• "Wordt het morgen beter?" (Will it become better tomorrow?)  
• "Hij is een beetje moe." (He is a little tired.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Wanneer is het feest? — Misschien vanavond? — Lisa wordt een beetje ongeduldig." (When is the party? — Maybe tonight? — Lisa is becoming a little impatient.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, directness is common. Asking "Wanneer?" without extra context can be seen as straightforward but is generally acceptable.

sentences.nl: Nou… dat is over een half uur.
sentences.en: Well... that's in half an hour.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Well… that is in about half an hour.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Nou" is often used to express a slight hesitation or to introduce a thought, similar to "well" in English.  
• "Dat is" translates to "that is," which is a simple present tense construction.  
• "Over een half uur" means "in about half an hour," where "over" is a preposition indicating time in the future.  
• Example phrases:  
  - "Over een week ben ik terug." (In a week, I will be back.)  
  - "Dat is mijn boek." (That is my book.)

## 3. Create a New Example

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The use of "nou" at the beginning of a sentence is quite common in Dutch conversational speech, often setting a casual or slightly informal tone. It doesn't always translate directly but serves to soften or introduce statements.

sentences.nl: Dan moet je opschieten.
sentences.en: Then you need to hurry.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Then must you hurry.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Moet" is the modal verb "must," which is used to express necessity or obligation.  
• "Opschieten" means "to hurry" and is commonly used in informal contexts.  
• The structure "Dan moet je..." (Then you must...) is used to suggest an action that should be taken next.  
• Examples:  
  - "Dan moet je luisteren." (Then you must listen.)  
  - "Dan moet je het proberen." (Then you must try it.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Dan moet je de trein halen." (Then you must catch the train.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, punctuality is generally valued, so being told to "opschieten" might reflect a common social expectation to be on time.

sentences.nl: Oh, is het al zo laat? — Eh… hoe loop ik naar het station? — Als je buiten komt, ga je naar rechts.
sentences.en: Oh, is it that late already? — Uh… how do I get to the station? — When you go outside, go right.

sentences.nl: Dan loop je steeds rechtdoor.
sentences.en: Then you keep walking straight ahead.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Then walk you continuously straight ahead.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Dan" is an adverb meaning "then," often used to indicate a sequence of actions.  
• "Loop je" is the verb "lopen" (to walk) conjugated for "je" (you), which means "you walk." The word order is inverted because it's a directive.  
• "Steeds" means "continuously" or "always," used to emphasize the constancy of the action.  
• "Rechtdoor" means "straight ahead," a compound of "recht" (straight) and "door" (through).

- Gebruik dan de trap. (Then use the stairs.)
- Hij loopt steeds sneller. (He walks increasingly faster.)
- Ga rechtdoor tot het einde van de straat. (Go straight ahead until the end of the street.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Dan neem je de tweede afslag links. (Then take the second left turn.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, walking and cycling directions often include terms like "rechtdoor," as biking and walking are popular modes of transportation.

sentences.nl: Bij de kerk ga je naar links.
sentences.en: At the church, you turn left.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• By the church go you to left.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Bij" is a preposition meaning "by" or "at," used to indicate location.  
• "Ga je" is the inversion of "je gaat" (you go), common in Dutch for commands or directions.  
• "Naar links" means "to the left," where "naar" indicates direction.  

Extra examples:  
• "Bij het station neem je de bus." (By the station, you take the bus.)  
• "Bij de rotonde ga je rechtdoor." (At the roundabout, you go straight ahead.)  
• "Je gaat naar rechts bij de stoplichten." (You go to the right at the traffic lights.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Bij het park ga je rechtdoor." (At the park, you go straight ahead.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Dutch cities often have churches as central landmarks, making them common reference points for giving directions.

• And then come you naturally at the station.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "En dan" is a conjunction used to indicate a sequence of events, similar to "and then" in English.  
• "Kom je vanzelf" uses the reflexive pronoun "je" to suggest that it will happen naturally or automatically. "Vanzelf" implies something happens without effort.  
• "Bij het station" means "at the station," where "bij" is a preposition indicating proximity or location.

• Extra Phrases:  
  - "En dan ga je rechtdoor." (And then you go straight ahead.)  
  - "Hij komt vanzelf tot rust." (He will naturally come to rest.)  
  - "We ontmoeten elkaar bij het café." (We meet each other at the café.)

sentences.nl: Eh… loop je niet even met mij mee? — Ik ben een beetje moe.
sentences.en: Uh... won't you walk with me for a bit? — I'm a little tired.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Eh… walk you not just with me along? — I am a little tired.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Loop je niet even met mij mee?" uses the structure of a question, starting with the verb "loop" (walk) followed by the subject "je" (you). The word "niet" (not) is used for negation. "Even" suggests a short or quick action, and "mee" implies accompanying someone.  
• "Ik ben een beetje moe" translates to "I am a little tired," using "ben" (am) for the first-person singular of "zijn" (to be) and "een beetje" (a little) as a common expression for slight amounts.

• Examples:  
  - "Kom je niet even met mij mee?" (Won't you come along with me?)  
  - "Ik ben een beetje hongerig." (I am a little hungry.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Zing je niet even met ons mee?" (Won't you sing along with us?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• (No cultural note is applicable here.)

sentences.nl: Ik ga slapen.
sentences.en: I am going to sleep.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I go sleep.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ik ga slapen" is in the present tense and uses the verb "gaan" (to go) followed by an infinitive verb "slapen" (to sleep). This structure is used to indicate a near future action or intention.  
• The sentence structure is: [Subject] + [Form of "gaan"] + [Infinitive verb].  
• Examples:  
  - Ik ga eten. (I am going to eat.)  
  - Wij gaan fietsen. (We are going to cycle.)  
  - Zij gaat werken. (She is going to work.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Ik ga studeren. (I am going to study.)

sentences.nl: ‘Eh… ik kan wel met je meelopen’, zegt Gianluca.
sentences.en: 'Uh... I can walk with you,' says Gianluca.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• "Eh… I can well with you walk along," says Gianluca.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The phrase "ik kan wel met je meelopen" combines modal verb "kan" (can) with "wel," which here implies willingness or a positive tone. "Met je meelopen" means "to walk along with you," where "meelopen" is a separable verb.  
• Separable verbs like "meelopen" split in main clauses: "Hij loopt met ons mee" (He walks along with us).  
• "Wel" can emphasize capability or willingness: "Ik kan wel helpen" (I can help for sure).  
• Use of direct speech: Direct speech is indicated by quotation marks and a comma before "zegt" (says).

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Eh… ik kan wel even wachten", zegt Anna. (Eh… I can wait for a moment, says Anna.)
